This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Wellington Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 8 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Wellington Intl Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/nz/wellington/NZWN.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

**Trader sentiment for Wellington’s peak temperature on August 9 centers on the narrow gap between 14 °C and 15 °C because short-range numerical weather prediction models and ensemble guidance show only modest differences in maximum surface temperature under similar synoptic patterns.** 

Wellington’s exposed coastal position on the Cook Strait makes temperatures highly sensitive to wind direction and speed: northerly or northwesterly flows advect milder maritime air, while southerly changes behind fronts introduce cooler air masses. Recent model runs indicate a transitional regime with variable winds and possible cloud breaks that allow modest daytime heating, keeping the daily maximum near the long-term August average of roughly 14 °C. 

Small forecast divergences—such as the exact timing of a frontal passage, boundary-layer mixing depth, or localized sea-breeze effects—can shift the peak by 1 °C, which explains the tight market split. Seasonal context from NIWA and developing El Niño signals favor near-average temperatures overall, but the 48-hour horizon for August 9 introduces limited uncertainty from model spread rather than major regime shifts. Official guidance currently leans toward a 13–14 °C maximum, yet the slight upside bias in trader probabilities reflects the potential for brief sunny intervals or a marginally warmer air mass to push the reading to 15 °C.
